title: Prefix of the return sweep
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $x$ be a word over the schedule alphabet. Fix a base configuration on $x$, an input-head position $p$, an integer budget-head position $b$, arbitrary budget and guide tapes, and natural numbers $B,j$ with $j\le 3B$. Starting in layout-return phase $0$ with unary head at $B$, unary tape containing $B$ markers, and guide head at $3B$, after $j$ steps the machine is in layout-return phase $j\bmod 3$, with unary head at $B-\lfloor j/3\rfloor$ and guide head at $3B-j$; the other configuration data, including all tape contents, are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
initial unary head is at $B$ on the unary tape with $B$ markers
replaced:
Let $j \le 3B$.  From layout-return phase $0$ with unary head at cell $B$ over the
unary tape with $B$ markers and guide head at cell $3B$ (over an arbitrary guide tape),
exactly $j$ steps lead to layout-return phase $j \bmod 3$ with unary head at
$B - \lfloor j/3 \rfloor$ and guide head at $3B - j$; no tape is written and all guide
marks are unchanged.
